name: struan

attributes.attribute: a harvest-bread and a name for the ritual cake
won by the best dancer and shared out
a darkened piece marks the devoted share

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Struan is a cross-reference in the encyclopedia to the entry CAKE. As a food, struan is a harvest-bread, one more name for the cake served at the lighting feasts. The cake at such a rite, sometimes called a bannock, was not mere food it had a part to play. It was set before all the people and won by the best dancer or athlete, who then broke it and shared it out. One piece of the cake was darkened with smoke, and the person who drew that share was said to be devoted. Some readers take the dark piece as a mark of a bygone offering of blood. In the Scottish islands a cake of this kind was baked for the harvest meaning, and the same name carried the bread of the year's close. So when the old text sends the reader to CAKE it points to the fuller record of the bread and its rite. The struan is that cake in its harvest form.
